documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PHYSICIAN NOTE
Arrival 02/24/2025 15:20

Chief complaint: painful blistering rash on the left side x 3 days.

HPI: 71-year-old woman on methotrexate and chronic prednisone for RA, with vulvar SCC treated in 2023, presents with a rash that started as a patch of red bumps on the left side of her trunk and turned into fluid-filled blisters, all in one strip wrapping toward her back. Burning pain. No fever. No recent illness. Says she has been very stressed looking after her husband, who has been unwell.

PMH: T2DM, HTN (on HCTZ among others), CKD 3b, osteoporosis with wrist fracture 2024, severe COPD, GERD, secondary hyperparathyroidism.
Meds: per pharmacy list - metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, omeprazole, prednisone, methotrexate, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol, aspirin, alendronate, calcium, vitamin D.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: within normal limits.

Exam: Grouped erythematous papules and vesicles on an erythematous base in a band along the left T8 dermatome, ending at the midline anteriorly and posteriorly without crossing. No lesions elsewhere on the skin. No ocular involvement. Lungs with diminished sounds, no distress.

Labs: HIV antibody negative. Fasting glucose 148. CBC unremarkable for her (white count and platelets normal, hemoglobin at her usual CKD level). ESR 20 mm/hr (normal <20).

Assessment: Herpes zoster, left T8 dermatome, in an immunosuppressed patient; localized, no dissemination.
Plan: valacyclovir 1 g every 12 hours for 7 days, renally dosed. Acetaminophen for pain. Keep lesions covered. Avoid contact with pregnant people and infants until crusted. PCP follow-up within a week; return for spreading rash, eye symptoms, fever or confusion.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Shingles Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED 2/24 for left T8 zoster; ED record reviewed (HIV negative, fasting glucose 148, ESR 20). Finished valacyclovir yesterday.

Pain is less - a 3/10 burn, worse at night. No new blisters after day 2 of treatment. No fever. Eyes fine. Taking acetaminophen twice a day.

She is worn down. Her husband is ill and she is his main help. She is not sleeping well. Denies feeling hopeless.

Exam: vitals as charted. Left T8 band of crusted lesions, no vesicles, no secondary infection, no spread past the midline.

A/P: Herpes zoster, healing well. Skin care, acetaminophen as needed. Shingles vaccine after full recovery - this spring. Caregiver strain acknowledged; gave her the area agency on aging number for respite resources. RTC May for diabetes.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Shingles fully healed; occasional twinge, no ongoing pain.

Diabetes: still above goal, fasting 150s on her meter. CKD: labs today. BP fine. No COPD flares this winter.

Colorectal screening: last colonoscopy 2016; given her lung disease she prefers stool testing to another colonoscopy - FIT kit given.

Exam: vitals as charted. Healed T8 area without scarring. Lungs distant. Regular. Feet intact.

Plan: labs, FIT. Shingles vaccine dose 1 next month at a nurse visit.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Released to portal with a note: no further colon testing needed this year.

documents.title: Shingles vaccine dose 1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1, L deltoid. Non-live vaccine, appropriate with methotrexate/prednisone. Zoster episode in February fully resolved. Warned about 1-2 days of arm soreness, tiredness or chills. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months - plan with fall vaccines.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body: Surveillance, 2.5 years after treatment of FIGO IB right vulvar SCC. Shingles in February noted. No vulvar itching or pain. Exam: no lesions, scar intact, groins without nodes, no lymphedema. NED. Return in 9 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.

Interval: zoster in February, healed. FIT negative in May. Gyn onc clear last week. No admissions.

Caregiving for husband continues. PHQ-9 4 - tired, some trouble sleeping, no anhedonia, no SI. Functional: independent, no falls since 1/2024.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs distant, no wheeze. Heart regular. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses present, skin intact.

Vaccines today: shingles dose 2, high-dose flu, updated COVID, Tdap (last 2015). Spread across both arms.
Labs today. RTC December.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology, 10/21/2025. CKD 3b continuing a slow decline; creatinine 1.7-1.8, eGFR low 30s. Albuminuria persists. Secondary HPT stable. Hemoglobin ~10.8. Potassium normal. Discussed with her what more rapid progression would look like and the general options for kidney replacement therapy if it ever came to that; she would want to consider dialysis. No changes now. If eGFR falls under 30, stop alendronate and reassess metformin. Return 1 year.

Outside Nephrology Group

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: RA follow-up 11/18/2025. Shingles in February while on MTX/prednisone, now vaccinated with recombinant zoster vaccine. Joints quiet. Renal function borderline for MTX; continue 15 mg weekly for now with labs every 3 months, will stop if eGFR drops below 30. Prednisone 10 mg unchanged. 12 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Routine. Nephrology and rheum letters reviewed - both keeping current meds with closer lab checks. September A1c 8.9. She is coping with caregiving. Breathing ok so far this winter. Vitals as charted; exam unchanged (distant breath sounds, regular rhythm, no edema, feet intact). BMP/CBC/LFTs today. RTC March.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated exam 12/9/2025: corrected VA 20/30 OD, 20/30 OS. Cataracts mild-moderate, she is not yet bothered. No diabetic retinopathy. No macular edema. Return 12 months.
